explanation: `var` is function-scoped, not block-scoped, so there is only one `i` shared by every iteration of the loop. By the time any click handler actually runs, the loop has already finished and `i` holds its final value (`buttons.length`). All handlers close over that same variable, so every one logs the same number instead of the index it was attached to. Using `let i` would create a fresh binding per iteration and fix it.
prompt: Users report every button logs the same number when clicked, no matter which one they press. What's the bug?
choices: `var i` is shared across all loop iterations, so every click handler closes over the same variable and logs its final value after the loop ends
addEventListener does not support anonymous functions as listeners, so the handlers silently fail to bind correctly
buttons.length is evaluated once before the loop, so buttons added to the DOM later never receive a click listener
The click event fires before `i` is incremented, so the first handler always logs undefined instead of 0
String concatenation with `+` coerces `i` to NaN inside console.log, so every handler prints the same NaN value
